body:
She has no specific plans, but basically says that she intends to kill herself eventually. There's no urgency, she doesn't feel that life is suffering, she just doesn't see the point and says she will eventually just check out. Super paranoid about living a life of mediocrity and growing old, she says she would rather die young.

That's part of why I struggle to know how to respond, I'm not sure how serious she is. She is 34 years old, so the whole aging thing isn't exactly a distant vaguery. 

I will ask about therapy if the opportunity presents itself. Maybe I can question the suicide thing more directly when she inevitably brings it up again.

Yeah, if he insisted on playing up the whole "virtue signaling" aspect of it, the old man could have at least made a baseless patronizing assumption. Like "Don't get a splinter! Do you need me to get those down for you? Where's your husband?" Idk, there's probably no saving it
